revision.comment: 仙台市にある7-8世紀の横穴墓群。1988年に発見、緊急発掘調査の後、破壊
revision.text:
[[Image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|thumb|240px|right|遺跡の現状。元は左を川上とする谷で、その斜面に横穴が埋もれていた（2008年）]] '''茂ヶ崎横穴墓群'''（もがさきよこあなぼぐん）は、7世紀後半から8世紀前半に作られた[[横穴墓]]群で、現在の[[宮城県]][[仙台市]][[太白区]]二ツ沢にある。[[1988年]]に[[東北工業大学]]二ツ沢キャンパスの造成工事注に発見され、25の横穴墓が確認・調査された。現存しない。
==立地== 茂ヶ崎は[[大年寺山]]の古名である。大年寺山の中腹では[[大年寺山横穴墓群]]、[[二ツ沢横穴墓群]]が見つかっており、茂ヶ崎横穴墓群や周辺の他の横穴墓群とあわせて[[向山横穴墓群]]という。茂ヶ崎横穴墓群が作られたのは、山の南斜面、小さな短い谷に面したところである。発見されたのは25だが、未発見のものがまだある可能性゛か高い。谷は埋め立てられ、[[東北工業大学]]二ツ沢キャンパスの駐車場になっており、元の地形を窺うことは難しい。
横穴墓が造成された時期には、南西に数キロはなれたところに当時の[[陸奥国|陸奥]][[国府]]である[[郡山遺跡]]があり、向山横穴墓群にはこれとの関連が指摘されているる。
==横穴の特徴== 重機を入れての工事中に発見されたため、発見時点で上部や全部が崩されていたものが多かった<ref>以下の解説は、特に記さない限り発掘調査報告書『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』による。</ref>。地上部への出口まで確認できたものは一つもない。壁にはノミのような工具の跡があり、玄室、玄門、羨道の三つの部分からなる。
玄室は遺体が置かれた部屋である。その平面は方形、隅が丸い方形、またはそれが歪んだ四辺形で、1辺は150センチメートルから340センチメートルの範囲におさまる。一部を除き、床に排水のための溝が彫られていた。5基は床の上に全面的に小石を敷き、5基は一部分に石を敷いた。
天井はドーム形かアーチ形で、高さは100センチメートルから218センチである。玄室への入り口部分は、そこに至る羨道より幅が狭い。それが玄門で、幅は60センチから85センチにおさまるが、40センチや135センチのような例外もある。高さまで判明したのは5基個しかないが、低いもので83センチ、高いものでは135あった。玄門には閉塞溝を備えたものが9基あった。床に細長い溝を切ったもので、そこに板を差し込んで扉にしたと考えられる。扉の閂を差し込んだと思われる穴も2基で見つかった。閉塞石は1基にあり、人の頭より大きな石を置いて通行を断っていた。
羨道は玄室まで続くトンネルで、幅75から170センチである。高さがわかったのは2基だけで、95センチと190センチであった。長さは不明である。
==出土遺物== 横穴からは、[[土師器]]8、[[須恵器]]17、玉類416、金属製品48が見つかった。
発掘された土師器は坏6、高坏1、甕1。須恵器は坏1、平瓶3、長頸壺6、長頸瓶3、短頸瓶1、甕3である。
[[勾玉]]は長さ3センチ前後の瑪瑙（[[メノウ]]）製が8、長さ1.7センチのガラス製が1で、計9見つかった。[[碧玉]]製の管玉<ref>以下はみな形による分類で、その形は字義が示す。例えば短いパイプのような形にカットされたのが管玉である。</ref>は、長さ2から4センチ程度のもの5つ見つかった。六角形やそろばん玉の形にカットした長さ1.2センチから2.6センチの[[水晶]]製切子玉が5つ、翡翠（[[ヒスイ]]）製の丸玉10、[[蛇紋岩]]製丸玉2、材質不明の丸玉2、琥珀（[[コハク]]）製の扁平な棗玉6、材質不明の棗玉2、黒い塗料を塗った材質不明（土製か）の臼玉7、その他臼玉5があった。しかしもっとも数が多いのは径3から4ミリのガラス製小玉で、329あった。5ミリ程度が7、1センチ程度のガラス玉は17である。いずれも紐・糸を通すための穴を開けている。
金属製装飾品として、銅に鍍金した耳輪が三つ、4号横穴からだけ出土した。
武器類としては、直刀5、刀装具1、鍔1見つかった。鉄鏃が18、弓の飾りにする両頭金具が11。刀子は6あった。
==人骨== 3号横穴では5体分以上の人骨の断片が出土した。1人は小児で、4人は男女の成人と推定された。
==発掘史== [[1988年]]（昭和63年）4月5日、東北工業大学の二ツ沢キャンパスの造成工事中に、穴と人骨が見つかった。後に人骨は数十年前のものと判明したが、横穴のほうは古代遺跡とわかり、仙台市教育委員会が緊急調査を実施した。4月7日、8日、11日から18日までの日程で、11基の穴が発掘調査された。そのうち1つは第2次世界大戦中の[[防空壕]]であった。調査を終了した当日に1基が見つかり、これをその日のうちに調査し終えた。
工事が再開された後、4月28日にまた横穴が5基見つかった。5月6日から16日の調査で、2次調査分は14基になったが、1次調査のときと比べ遺存状態は悪かった。横穴の端だけが検出されたものもある。これら調査の終了後、遺跡は破壊された。
==脚注== <references />
==参考文献== *仙台市教育委員会『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』（仙台市文化財調査報告書第130集）、仙台市、1989年。
{{DEFAULTSORT:もかさきよこあなほくん}} [[Category:宮城県の古墳]] [[Category:太白区]]

茂ヶ崎は[[大年寺山]]の古名である。大年寺山の中腹では[[大年寺山横穴墓群]]、[[二ツ沢横穴墓群]]が見つかっており、茂ヶ崎横穴墓群や周辺の他の横穴墓群とあわせて[[向山横穴墓群]]という。茂ヶ崎横穴墓群が作られたのは、山の南斜面、小さな短い谷に面したところである。発見されたのは25だが、未発見のものがまだある可能性が高い。谷は埋め立てられ、[[東北工業大学]]二ツ沢キャンパスの駐車場になっており、元の地形を窺うことは難しい。 横穴墓が造成された時期には、南西に数キロはなれたところに当時の[[陸奥国|陸奥]][[国府]]である[[郡山遺跡]]があり、向山横穴墓群にはこれとの関連が指摘されている。 ==横穴の特徴== 重機を入れての工事中に発見されたため、発見時点で上部や全部が崩されていたものが多かった以下の解説は、特に記さない限り発掘調査報告書『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』による。。地上部への出口まで確認できたものは一つもない。壁にはノミのような工具の跡があり、玄室、玄門、羨道の三つの部分からなる。 玄室は遺体が置かれた部屋である。その平面は方形、隅が丸い方形、またはそれが歪んだ四辺形で、1辺は150センチメートルから340センチメートルの範囲におさまる。一部を除き、床に排水のための溝が掘られていた。5基は床の上に全面的に小石を敷き、5基は一部分に小石を敷いた。天井はドーム形かアーチ形で、高さは100センチメートルから218センチである。 玄室への入り口部分は、そこに至る羨道より幅が狭い。それが玄門で、ほとんどの横穴では幅は60センチから85センチにおさまるが、40センチや135センチのような例外もある。高さまで判明したのは5基個しかないが、低いもので83センチ、高いものでは135あった。玄門には閉塞溝を備えたものが9基あった。床に細長い溝を切ったもので、そこに板を差し込んで扉にしたと考えられる。扉の閂を差し込んだと思われる穴も2基で見つかった。閉塞石は1基にあり、人の頭より大きな石を置いて通行を断っていた。 羨道は玄室まで続くトンネルで、幅75から170センチである。高さがわかったのは2基だけで、95センチと190センチであった。長さは不明である。 ==出土遺物== 横穴からは、[[土師器]]8、[[須恵器]]17、玉類416、金属製品48が見つかった。 発掘された土師器は坏6、高坏1、甕1。須恵器は坏1、平瓶3、長頸壺6、長頸瓶3、短頸瓶1、甕3である。 [[勾玉]]は長さ3センチ前後の瑪瑙（[[メノウ]]）製が8、長さ1.7センチのガラス製が1で、計9見つかった。[[碧玉]]製の管玉以下はみな形による分類で、その形は字義が示す。例えば短いパイプのような形にカットされたのが管玉である。は、長さ2から4センチ程度のもの5つ見つかった。六角形やそろばん玉の形にカットした長さ1.2センチから2.6センチの[[水晶]]製切子玉が5つ、翡翠（[[ヒスイ]]）製の丸玉10、[[蛇紋岩]]製丸玉2、材質不明の丸玉2、琥珀（[[コハク]]）製の扁平な棗玉6、材質不明の棗玉2、黒い塗料を塗った材質不明（土製か）の臼玉7、その他臼玉5があった。しかしもっとも数が多いのは径3から4ミリのガラス製小玉で、329あった。5ミリ程度が7、1センチ程度のガラス玉は17である。これらの玉類には、いずれも紐・糸を通すための孔がある。 金属製装飾品として、銅に鍍金した耳輪が三つ、4号横穴からだけ出土した。 武器類としては、直刀5、刀装具1、鍔1見つかった。鉄鏃が18、弓の飾りにする両頭金具が11。刀子は6あった。 ==人骨== 3号横穴では5体分以上の人骨の断片が出土した。1人は小児で、4人は男女の成人と推定された。 ==発掘史== [[1988年]]（昭和63年）4月5日、東北工業大学の二ツ沢キャンパスの造成工事中に、穴と人骨が見つかった。後に人骨は数十年前のものと判明したが、横穴のほうは古代遺跡とわかり、仙台市教育委員会が緊急調査を実施した。4月7日、8日、11日から18日までの日程で、11基の穴が発掘調査された。そのうち1つは第2次世界大戦中の[[防空壕]]であった。調査を終了した当日に1基が見つかり、これをその日のうちに調査し終えた。 工事が再開された後、4月28日にまた横穴が5基見つかった。5月6日から16日の調査で、2次調査分は14基になったが、1次調査のときと比べ遺存状態は悪かった。横穴の端だけが検出されたものもある。これら調査の終了後、遺跡は破壊された。 ==脚注== ==参考文献== *仙台市教育委員会『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』（仙台市文化財調査報告書第130集）、仙台市、1989年。 {{日本の古墳| 名称=茂ヶ崎横穴墓群| 所在地=宮城県仙台市太白区二ツ沢| 位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|}}| 形状=横穴墓25基（非現存）| 築造年代=7世紀後半 - 8世紀前半| 規模=| 被葬者=| 史跡指定=| 出土品=土師器、須恵器、玉類、金属製品| 画像=[[Image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
遺跡の現状。元は左を川上とする谷で、その斜面に横穴が埋もれていた（2008年）|}} '''茂ヶ崎横穴墓群'''（もがさきよこあなぼぐん）は、[[7世紀]]後半から[[8世紀]]前半に作られた[[横穴墓]]群で、現在の[[宮城県]][[仙台市]][[太白区]]二ツ沢にある。[[1988年]]に[[東北工業大学]]二ツ沢キャンパスの造成工事中に発見され、25の横穴墓が確認・調査された。現存しない。 ==立地== 茂ヶ崎は[[大年寺山]]の古名である。大年寺山の中腹では[[大年寺山横穴墓群]]、[[二ツ沢横穴墓群]]が見つかっており、茂ヶ崎横穴墓群や周辺の他の横穴墓群とあわせて[[向山横穴墓群]]という。茂ヶ崎横穴墓群が作られたのは、山の南斜面、小さな短い谷に面したところである。発見されたのは25基だが、未発見のものがまだある可能性が高い。谷は埋め立てられ、[[東北工業大学]]二ツ沢キャンパスの駐車場になっており、元の地形を窺うことは難しい。 横穴墓が造成された時期には、南西に数キロメートルはなれたところに当時の[[陸奥国|陸奥]][[国府]]である[[郡山遺跡]]があり、向山横穴墓群にはこれとの関連が指摘されている。 ==横穴の特徴== [[重機]]を入れての工事中に発見されたため、発見時点で上部や全部が崩されていたものが多かった以下の解説は、特に記さない限り発掘調査報告書『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』による。。地上部への出口まで確認できたものは一つもない。壁にはノミのような[[工具]]の跡があり、[[玄室]]、玄門、[[羨道]]の三つの部分からなる。 玄室は遺体が置かれた部屋である。その平面は方形、隅が丸い方形、またはそれが歪んだ四辺形で、1辺は150センチメートルから340センチメートルの範囲におさまる。一部を除き、床に排水のための溝が掘られていた。5基は床の上に全面的に小石を敷き、5基は一部分に小石を敷いた。天井はドーム形かアーチ形で、高さは100センチから218センチメートルである。 玄室への入り口部分は、そこに至る羨道より幅が狭い。それが玄門で、ほとんどの横穴では幅は60センチから85センチメートルにおさまるが、40センチや135センチメートルのような例外もある。高さまで判明したのは5基個しかないが、低いもので83センチ、高いものでは135センチメートルあった。玄門には閉塞溝を備えたものが9基あった。床に細長い溝を切ったもので、そこに板を差し込んで扉にしたと考えられる。扉の閂を差し込んだと思われる穴も2基で見つかった。閉塞石は1基にあり、人の頭より大きな石を置いて通行を断っていた。 羨道は玄室まで続くトンネルで、幅75から170センチメートルである。高さがわかったのは2基だけで、95センチと190センチメートルであった。長さは不明である。 ==出土遺物== 横穴からは、[[土師器]]8、[[須恵器]]17、玉類416、金属製品48が見つかった。 発掘された土師器は坏6、高坏1、甕1。須恵器は坏1、平瓶3、長頸壺6、長頸瓶3、短頸瓶1、甕3である。 [[勾玉]]は長さ3センチ前後の瑪瑙（[[メノウ]]）製が8、長さ1.7センチのガラス製が1で、計9見つかった。[[碧玉]]製の管玉以下はみな形による分類で、その形は字義が示す。例えば短いパイプのような形にカットされたのが管玉である。は、長さ2から4センチ程度のもの5つ見つかった。六角形やそろばん玉の形にカットした長さ1.2センチから2.6センチの[[水晶]]製切子玉が5つ、翡翠（[[ヒスイ]]）製の丸玉10、[[蛇紋岩]]製丸玉2、材質不明の丸玉2、琥珀（[[コハク]]）製の扁平な棗玉6、材質不明の棗玉2、黒い塗料を塗った材質不明（土製か）の臼玉7、その他臼玉5があった。しかしもっとも数が多いのは径3から4ミリのガラス製小玉で、329あった。5ミリ程度が7、1センチ程度のガラス玉は17である。これらの玉類には、いずれも紐・糸を通すための孔がある。 金属製装飾品として、銅に鍍金した耳輪が三つ、4号横穴からだけ出土した。 武器類としては、[[直刀]]5点、刀装具1点、[[鍔]]1点が見つかった。[[鉄鏃]]が18点、弓の飾りにする両頭金具が11点あり、[[刀子]]は6点あった。 ==人骨== 3号横穴では5体分以上の人骨の断片が出土した。1人は小児で、4人は男女の[[成人]]と推定された。 ==発掘史== [[1988年]]（昭和63年）4月5日、東北工業大学の二ツ沢キャンパスの造成工事中に、穴と人骨が見つかった。後に人骨は数十年前のものと判明したが、横穴のほうは古代遺跡とわかり、仙台市教育委員会が緊急調査を実施した。4月7日、8日、11日から18日までの日程で、11基の穴が発掘調査された。そのうち1つは第2次世界大戦中の[[防空壕]]であった。調査を終了した当日に1基が見つかり、これをその日のうちに調査し終えた。 工事が再開された後、4月28日にまた横穴が5基見つかった。5月6日から16日の調査で、2次調査分は14基になったが、1次調査のときと比べ遺存状態は悪かった。横穴の端だけが検出されたものもある。これら調査の終了後、遺跡は破壊された。 ==脚注== {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} ==参考文献== [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html 茂ケ崎横穴墓群] {{DEFAULTSORT:もかさきよこあなほくん}} [[Category:宮城県の古墳]] [[Category:仙台市の歴史]] [[Category:太白区]]

[[1988年]]（昭和63年）4月5日、東北工業大学の二ツ沢キャンパスの造成工事中に、穴と人骨が見つかった。後に人骨は数十年前のものと判明したが、横穴のほうは古代遺跡とわかり、仙台市教育委員会が緊急調査を実施した。4月7日、8日、11日から18日までの日程で、11基の穴が発掘調査された。そのうち1つは第2次世界大戦中の[[防空壕]]であった。調査を終了した当日に1基が見つかり、これをその日のうちに調査し終えた。 工事が再開された後、4月28日にまた横穴が5基見つかった。5月6日から16日の調査で、2次調査分は14基になったが、1次調査のときと比べ遺存状態は悪かった。横穴の端だけが検出されたものもある。これら調査の終了後、遺跡は破壊された。 ==脚注== {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} ==参考文献== {{日本の古墳| 名称=茂ヶ崎横穴墓群| 所在地=宮城県仙台市太白区二ツ沢| 位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|}}| 形状=横穴墓25基（非現存）| 築造年代=7世紀後半 - 8世紀前半| 規模=| 被葬者=| 史跡指定=| 出土品=土師器、須恵器、玉類、金属製品| 画像=[[Image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
遺跡の現状。元は左を川上とする谷で、その斜面に横穴が埋もれていた（2008年）|}} '''茂ヶ崎横穴墓群'''（もがさきよこあなぼぐん）は、[[7世紀]]後半から[[8世紀]]前半に作られた[[横穴墓]]群で、現在の[[宮城県]][[仙台市]][[太白区]][[二ツ沢]]にある。[[1988年]]に[[東北工業大学]]二ツ沢キャンパスの造成工事中に発見され、25の横穴墓が確認・調査された。現存しない。 ==立地== 茂ヶ崎は[[大年寺山]]の古名である。大年寺山の中腹では[[大年寺山横穴墓群]]、[[二ツ沢横穴墓群]]が見つかっており、茂ヶ崎横穴墓群や周辺の他の横穴墓群とあわせて[[向山横穴墓群]]という。茂ヶ崎横穴墓群が作られたのは、山の南斜面、小さな短い谷に面したところである。発見されたのは25基だが、未発見のものがまだある可能性が高い。谷は埋め立てられ、[[東北工業大学]]二ツ沢キャンパスの駐車場になっており、元の地形を窺うことは難しい。 横穴墓が造成された時期には、南西に数キロメートルはなれたところに当時の[[陸奥国|陸奥]][[国府]]である[[郡山遺跡]]があり、向山横穴墓群にはこれとの関連が指摘されている。 ==横穴の特徴== [[重機]]を入れての工事中に発見されたため、発見時点で上部や全部が崩されていたものが多かった以下の解説は、特に記さない限り発掘調査報告書『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』による。。地上部への出口まで確認できたものは一つもない。壁にはノミのような[[工具]]の跡があり、[[玄室]]、玄門、[[羨道]]の三つの部分からなる。 玄室は遺体が置かれた部屋である。その平面は方形、隅が丸い方形、またはそれが歪んだ四辺形で、1辺は150センチメートルから340センチメートルの範囲におさまる。一部を除き、床に排水のための溝が掘られていた。5基は床の上に全面的に小石を敷き、5基は一部分に小石を敷いた。天井はドーム形かアーチ形で、高さは100センチから218センチメートルである。 玄室への入り口部分は、そこに至る羨道より幅が狭い。それが玄門で、ほとんどの横穴では幅は60センチから85センチメートルにおさまるが、40センチや135センチメートルのような例外もある。高さまで判明したのは5基個しかないが、低いもので83センチ、高いものでは135センチメートルあった。玄門には閉塞溝を備えたものが9基あった。床に細長い溝を切ったもので、そこに板を差し込んで扉にしたと考えられる。扉の閂を差し込んだと思われる穴も2基で見つかった。閉塞石は1基にあり、人の頭より大きな石を置いて通行を断っていた。 羨道は玄室まで続くトンネルで、幅75から170センチメートルである。高さがわかったのは2基だけで、95センチと190センチメートルであった。長さは不明である。 ==出土遺物== 横穴からは、[[土師器]]8、[[須恵器]]17、玉類416、金属製品48が見つかった。 発掘された土師器は坏6、高坏1、甕1。須恵器は坏1、平瓶3、長頸壺6、長頸瓶3、短頸瓶1、甕3である。 [[勾玉]]は長さ3センチ前後の瑪瑙（[[メノウ]]）製が8、長さ1.7センチのガラス製が1で、計9見つかった。[[碧玉]]製の管玉以下はみな形による分類で、その形は字義が示す。例えば短いパイプのような形にカットされたのが管玉である。は、長さ2から4センチ程度のもの5つ見つかった。六角形やそろばん玉の形にカットした長さ1.2センチから2.6センチの[[水晶]]製切子玉が5つ、翡翠（[[ヒスイ]]）製の丸玉10、[[蛇紋岩]]製丸玉2、材質不明の丸玉2、琥珀（[[コハク]]）製の扁平な棗玉6、材質不明の棗玉2、黒い塗料を塗った材質不明（土製か）の臼玉7、その他臼玉5があった。しかしもっとも数が多いのは径3から4ミリのガラス製小玉で、329あった。5ミリ程度が7、1センチ程度のガラス玉は17である。これらの玉類には、いずれも紐・糸を通すための孔がある。 工事が再開された後、4月28日にまた横穴が5基見つかった。5月6日から16日の調査で、2次調査分は14基になったが、1次調査のときと比べ遺存状態は悪かった。横穴の端だけが検出されたものもある。これら調査の終了後、遺跡は破壊された。 ==脚注== {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} ==参考文献== == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with a high concentration in [[Southern Kantō]]. The northern limit is thought to be in northern [[Miyagi Prefecture]]. Approximately 3,000 examples exist in [[Shizuoka Prefecture]].
=== Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Yamahata Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|山畑横穴群}} ({{ill|Ōsaki, Miyagi|ja|大崎市}}, [[Miyagi Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site, 26 tombs * {{ill|Atagoyama Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|愛宕山横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Taihaku-ku, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}) * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|茂ヶ崎横穴墓群}} (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - 25 tombs, no longer extant * {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|宗禅寺横穴墓群}} (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) * {{ill|Kiyotosaku Yokoguchi|ja|清戸迫横穴墓}} ({{ill|Futaba, Fukushima|ja|双葉町}}, [[Fukushima Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site, over 300 tombs * {{ill|Izumizaki Yokoguchi|ja|泉崎横穴墓}} ({{ill|Nishishirakawa District|ja|西白河郡}}, {{ill|Izumizaki, Fukushima|ja|泉崎村}}) - National Historic Site * {{ill|Nakada Yokoguchi|ja|中田横穴}} ({{ill|Iwaki, Fukushima|ja|いわき市}}) - National Historic Site * {{ill|Hayama Yokoguchi|ja|羽山横穴}} ({{ill|Minamisōma|ja|南相馬市}}, Fukushima Prefecture) - National Historic Site * {{ill|Wada Daibutsu and Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|和田大仏及び横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Sukagawa|ja|須賀川市}}, Fukushima Prefecture) - Municipal Historic Site
=== Kantō Region === * {{ill|Jūgorō-ana Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|十五郎穴横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Hitachinaka, Ibaraki|ja|ひたちなか市}}, [[Ibaraki Prefecture]]) - Over 300 tombs * {{ill|Karagoshō Yokoguchi|ja|唐御所横穴}} ({{ill|Nasukaragawa, Tochigi|ja|那珂川町}}, [[Tochigi Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site, part of the Hokōda and Wami Yokoguchi Clusters * {{ill|Nagaoka Hyakka|ja|長岡百穴古墳}} ({{ill|Utsunomiya|ja|宇都宮市}}, Tochigi Prefecture) - 52 tombs * {{ill|Yoshimi Hyakka|ja|吉見百穴}} ({{ill|Yoshimi, Saitama|ja|吉見町}}, [[Saitama Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site, over 200 tombs * {{ill|Kuroiwa Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|黒岩横穴墓群}} (Yoshimi, Saitama) - Over 30 tombs * {{ill|Jūrō Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|十郎横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Hatoyama, Saitama|ja|鳩山町}}, Saitama) - 3 tombs * {{ill|Takinojō Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|滝之城横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Tokorozawa|ja|所沢市}}, Saitama) - 9 tombs * {{ill|Kitaakitsu Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|北秋津横穴墓群}} (Tokorozawa, Saitama) - 8 tombs * {{ill|Bikuniyama Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|比丘尼山横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Higashimatsuyama|ja|東松山市}}, Saitama) - Over 50 tombs * {{ill|Takane Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|高根横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Kumagaya|ja|熊谷市}}, Saitama) - Municipal Historic Site * {{ill|Nagara Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|長柄横穴群}} ({{ill|Nagara, Chiba|ja|長柄町}}, [[Chiba Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site, over 300 tombs * {{ill|Deyama Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|出山横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, [[Tokyo]]) - Metropolitan Historic Site, 10 tombs * {{ill|Nakawada Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|中和田横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Tama, Tokyo|ja|多摩市}}, Tokyo) - 14 tombs * {{ill|Todoroki Ravine Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|谷沢川横穴群}} ({{ill|Setagaya|ja|世田谷区}}, Tokyo) * {{ill|Ekoda Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|荏子田横穴}} ({{ill|Aoba-ku, Yokohama|ja|青葉区}}, {{ill|Yokohama|ja|横浜市}}, [[Kanagawa Prefecture]]) - Municipal Historic Site, 2 tombs * {{ill|Ichigao Yokoguchi Kofun Cluster|ja|市ヶ尾横穴古墳群}} (Aoba-ku, Yokohama) - Prefectural Historic Site, 19 tombs * {{ill|Kanazawa River Basin Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|㹨川流域横穴墓群}} (Kamakura-style tomb concentration) ** {{ill|Matsugasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|松ヶ崎横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Kōnan-ku, Yokohama|ja|港南区}}, Yokohama) - Municipal Historic Site, 8 tombs ** {{ill|Shichishiyama Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|七石山横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Sakae-ku, Yokohama|ja|栄区}}, Yokohama) - Over 100 tombs originally ** {{ill|Miyanomae Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|宮ノ前横穴墓群}} (Sakae-ku, Yokohama) - 23 tombs ** {{ill|Hikoshigaoka Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|ひこしヶ谷横穴墓群}} (Sakae-ku, Yokohama) - 12 tombs
=== Tokai Region === * {{ill|Kashiya Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|柏谷横穴群}} ({{ill|Kannami|ja|函南町}}, [[Shizuoka Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site, 106 tombs * {{ill|Kitaema Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|北江間横穴群}} ({{ill|Izunokuni|ja|伊豆の国市}}, Shizuoka) - National Historic Site, 101 tombs * {{ill|Eura Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|江浦横穴群}} ({{ill|Numazu|ja|沼津市}}, Shizuoka) - Prefectural Historic Site, 92 tombs
=== Hokuriku Region === * {{ill|Hōōzan Yokoguchi Kofun|ja|法皇山横穴古墳}} ({{ill|Kaga, Ishikawa|ja|加賀市}}, [[Ishikawa Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site, over 150 tombs
=== Kinki Region === * {{ill|Takaida Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|高井田横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Kashiwara, Osaka|ja|柏原市}}, [[Osaka Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site, over 200 tombs * {{ill|Anfukuji Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|安福寺横穴群}} (Kashiwara, Osaka) - 32 tombs
=== Chūgoku Region === * {{ill|Jūōmen Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|十王免横穴群}} ({{ill|Matsue|ja|松江市}}, [[Shimane Prefecture]]) - 37 tombs * {{ill|Kitsunedani Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|狐谷横穴墓群}} (Matsue, Shimane) - 16 tombs * {{ill|Kamikonishi Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|上塩冶横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Izumo, Shimane|ja|出雲市}}, Shimane) * {{ill|Takatsuku Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|高津久横穴墓群}} ({{ill|Chibu, Shimane|ja|知夫村}}, [[Oki District]])
=== Kyushu Region === * {{ill|Takenami Site|ja|竹並遺跡}} ({{ill|Yukuhashi|ja|行橋市}}, [[Fukuoka Prefecture]]) - Over 1,000 tombs * {{ill|Shiroyama Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|城山横穴群}} ({{ill|Fukuchi, Fukuoka|ja|福智町}}, Fukuoka) - National Historic Site, over 200 tombs * {{ill|Mizumachi Site|ja|水町遺跡}} ({{ill|Nōgata|ja|直方市}}, Fukuoka) - Prefectural Historic Site, over 40 tombs * {{ill|Kozuki Yokoguchi|ja|古月横穴}} ({{ill|Kurate, Fukuoka|ja|鞍手町}}, Fukuoka) - National Historic Site * {{ill|Ishinuki Nagino Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|石貫ナギノ横穴群}} ({{ill|Tamana|ja|玉名市}}, [[Kumamoto Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site * {{ill|Ishinuki Anakanon Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|石貫穴観音横穴群}} (Tamana, Kumamoto) - National Historic Site * {{ill|Nabeta Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|鍋田横穴群}} ({{ill|Yamaga, Kumamoto|ja|山鹿市}}, Kumamoto) - National Historic Site, 60 tombs * {{ill|Ōmura Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|大村横穴群}} ({{ill|Hitoyoshi|ja|人吉市}}, Kumamoto) - National Historic Site, 27 tombs * {{ill|Yokkaichi Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|四日市横穴群}} ({{ill|Usa|ja|宇佐市}}, [[Ōita Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site, 161 tombs * {{ill|Takio Hyakka Yokoguchi Kofun Cluster|ja|滝尾百穴横穴古墳群}} ({{ill|Ōita, Ōita|ja|大分市}}, Ōita) - Municipal Historic Site, 75 tombs * {{ill|Hasunogaike Yokoguchi Cluster|ja|蓮ヶ池横穴群}} ({{ill|Miyazaki, Miyazaki|ja|宮崎市}}, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]]) - National Historic Site

{{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | Image = [[Image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|ja|横穴墓}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the {{ill|Koriyama Ruins|ja|郡山遺跡}}, was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ** [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - 25 tombs, no longer extant * {{ill|Sōzenji Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:宗禅寺横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) * {{ill|Kiyotosaku Yokoguchi|en}}[[ja:清戸迫横穴墓]] ({{ill|Futaba, Fukushima|en}}[[ja:双葉町]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]) - Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|ja|横穴墓}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the {{ill|Koriyama Ruins|ja|郡山遺跡}}, was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ** [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | Image = [[Image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|ja|横穴墓}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ** [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ** [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | Image = [[Image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|ja|横穴墓}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ** [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | Image = [[Image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|ja|横穴墓}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ** [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ** [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | Image = [[Image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|ja|横穴墓}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ** [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) -
