{{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | image = [[image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道|1=endō|lt=endō (tomb entrance)}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Yokoguchi Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Yokoguchi Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | image = [[image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道|1=endō|lt=endō (tomb entrance)}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | image = [[image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道|1=endō|lt=endō (tomb entrance)}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道|1=endō|lt=endō (tomb entrance)}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | image = [[image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道|1=endō|lt=endō (tomb entrance)}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | image = [[image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道|1=endō|lt=endō (tomb entrance)}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | image = [[image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道|1=endō|lt=endō (tomb entrance)}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - {{Infobox Japanese burial mound| Name = Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster | Location = {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, Futatsuzawa | Coordinates = {{Coord|38|14|2|N|140|52|21|E|display=inline,title}} | Shape = Cave tombs (25 confirmed, no longer extant) | Construction period = Late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} – Early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} | Scale = | Interred individuals = | Historic site designation = | Excavated artifacts = {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, beads, metal objects | image = [[image:Mogasaki Yokoana Bogun Ato.jpg|250px]]
Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道|1=endō|lt=endō (tomb entrance)}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) - Current state of the site. Originally, the valley sloped leftward toward the river, with cave tombs buried in its slope (2008). | }} '''Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster''' (茂ヶ崎横穴墓群, Mogasaki Yokoana Bōgun) is a group of {{ill|cave tombs|lt=Cave tombs|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}} constructed between the late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} and early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}}, located in present-day {{ill|Futatsuzawa, Sendai|ja|二ツ沢}}, {{ill|Taihaku Ward, Sendai|ja|太白区}}, {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|ja|宮城県}}, Japan. It was discovered in [[1988]] during land development for {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, where 25 cave tombs were confirmed and investigated. The tombs are no longer extant. == Location == "Mogasaki" is the ancient name for {{ill|Mount Ōtōji|ja|大年寺山}}. On the slopes of this mountain, the {{ill|Ōtōjiyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|大年寺山横穴墓群}} and {{ill|Futatsuzawa Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|二ツ沢横穴墓群}} have been found. Together with the Mogasaki cluster and other nearby cave tombs, they are collectively called the {{ill|Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster|ja|向山横穴墓群}}. The Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster was built on the southern slope of the mountain, facing a small, short valley. While 25 tombs were identified, there is a strong possibility that additional, undiscovered tombs remain. The valley has since been filled in and turned into a parking lot for the {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}}'s Futatsuzawa Campus, making it difficult to discern the original landscape. At the time these cave tombs were constructed, the provincial capital of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}, the [[:en:Sendai_Kōriyama_Kanga_ruins|Kōriyama Kanga ruins]], was located several kilometers to the southwest. The Mukōyama Cave Tomb Cluster is believed to be associated with this provincial center. == Features of the Tombs == The tombs were discovered during heavy machinery excavation, resulting in severe damage to many of them by the time they were identified.Unless otherwise specified, this section is based on the excavation report "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』). None of the tombs were found intact from entrance to burial chamber. Chisel-like tool marks were observed on the walls, and each tomb consisted of a {{ill|burial chamber|ja|玄室}}, {{ill|gate|ja|玄門}}, and {{ill|entrance passage|ja|羨道|1=endō|lt=endō (tomb entrance)}}. The burial chambers, where the deceased were placed, had floor plans that were either square, rounded-square, or irregular quadrilaterals. Their dimensions ranged from 150 cm to 340 cm per side. Most chambers, except for a few, contained drainage channels carved into the floor. Five tombs had small stones covering the entire floor, while another five had partial stone coverings. The ceilings were either domed or arched, with heights ranging from 100 cm to 218 cm. The burial chamber entrances (玄門) were narrower than the entrance passages (羨道). Most were between 60 cm and 85 cm wide, though some measured as small as 40 cm or as wide as 135 cm. Only five tombs had confirmed entrance heights, which ranged from 83 cm to 135 cm. Nine tombs had blocking grooves in the floor, where wooden boards were likely inserted to seal the chamber. Two tombs contained holes that might have been used to insert locking bars for the doors. One tomb had a blocking stone larger than a human head to prevent passage. The entrance passages (羨道) leading to the burial chambers varied in width from 75 cm to 170 cm. Only two tombs had measurable passage heights—95 cm and 190 cm. The original lengths of the passages remain unknown. == Excavated Artifacts == Artifacts recovered from the site include eight {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, seventeen {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, 416 beads, and 48 metal objects. The excavated Haji ware consisted of six small bowls (坏), one tall-stemmed bowl (高坏), and one jar (甕). The Sue ware included one small bowl (坏), three flat bottles (平瓶), six long-necked jars (長頸壺), three long-necked bottles (長頸瓶), one short-necked bottle (短頸瓶), and three jars (甕). Among the beads, there were eight agate (メノウ) {{ill|Magatama|ja|勾玉}}, each approximately 3 cm long, and one 1.7 cm-long glass magatama. Five jasper (碧玉) {{ill|Tube beads|ja|管玉}} measuring 2 to 4 cm long were also recovered. Additionally, there were five quartz (水晶) cut beads (切子玉) shaped as hexagonal or abacus-style, ten jade (ヒスイ) round beads, two serpentine (蛇紋岩) round beads, and two round beads of unknown material. There were six flat amber (コハク) beads (棗玉) and two more of unidentified material. Seven unidentified beads, possibly earthenware with black paint, were found, along with five additional unspecified beads. The majority of the beads were small glass beads (小玉) measuring 3–4 mm in diameter (329 total), with seven measuring around 5 mm and seventeen measuring approximately 1 cm. All beads contained holes for stringing. Three gilded copper earrings were recovered from Tomb No. 4. Weapons included five straight swords (直刀), one sword fitting, and one guard (鍔). Eighteen iron arrowheads (鉄鏃), eleven decorative metal fittings for bows, and six knives (刀子) were also found. == Human Remains == Fragments of at least five individuals’ skeletal remains were recovered from Tomb No. 3. One individual was a child, while the other four were adults of both genders. == Excavation History == On April 5, [[1988]] (Shōwa 63), construction at the Futatsuzawa Campus of {{ill|Tohoku Institute of Technology|ja|東北工業大学}} revealed a tomb and human bones. Although the bones were later identified as relatively recent (a few decades old), the tomb itself was determined to be an ancient site, prompting the Sendai City Board of Education to conduct an emergency excavation. The first survey took place on April 7, 8, and from April 11 to 18, during which eleven tombs were excavated. One of these was identified as a World War II-era air-raid shelter. On the final day of the excavation, an additional tomb was discovered and examined the same day. Following the resumption of construction, another five tombs were found on April 28. The second phase of the survey took place from May 6 to 16, during which a total of fourteen additional tombs were excavated. Compared to the first phase, these tombs were in worse condition, with some only partially identifiable. After the surveys concluded, the site was destroyed. == References == {{reflist}} == Further Reading == * Sendai City Board of Education, "Sendai City Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster" (『仙台市茂ヶ崎横穴墓群』), Sendai Cultural Property Research Report No. 130, 1989. == External Links == * [http://www.city.sendai.jp/Category/bunka/02.html Cultural Heritage of Sendai] ({{ill|Sendai City Board of Education|ja|仙台市教育委員会}}) ''' [http://www.city.sendai.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/iseki/c0000000117.html Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster] [[Category:Ancient burial sites in Miyagi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Taihaku Ward, Sendai]] [[Category:Cave tombs in Japan]] == Distribution and Notable Cave Tomb Tombs == These tombs are found from Kyushu through San'in, Kinki, Hokuriku, and Tokai, with * {{ill|Mogasaki Cave Tomb Cluster|en}}[[ja:茂ヶ崎横穴墓群]] (Taihaku-ku, Sendai) -
